components.name: CareAgents
components.description: A patient's health assistant that answers a clinic's check-in request from their records, with per-item consent. Answers are encrypted in the browser and not stored by CareAgents.
components.notes: Sign in on the wallet page with an emailed code, then pick the synthetic test patient when the wallet offers it (self-serve, no real data). Supports the three minimum scenarios: share records and insurance (US Core, C4DIC Coverage), PHQ-2 inline, decline an item. Also answers short forms inline (up to 30 questions); optional questions it cannot answer are shown to the patient as not sent, and a required one it cannot answer means the whole form is not answered. Records are checked against US Core before they are sent, and any that fail are held back. Responses are capped at about 400 KB, so the large-response scenario is not supported yet. Testing guide: https://healthclaw.io/static/connectathon/careagents-wallet.html

components.name: RX Genie
components.description: A community pharmacy's check-in counter: asks the patient's wallet for demographics, medications, allergies, problems, immunizations, the insurance card, and the PHQ-2, and shows each item's status and contents.
components.notes: Web page, no sign-in. Pick a request under "What to ask for": "Share records" (scenario 1; decline Immunizations in the wallet for scenario 3), "Fill in a form" (PHQ-2 inline, scenario 2), "Pharmacy visit" (both), or one of the organizers' test requests, loaded live from /connectathon/requests/. Passed against the SMART Testing Wallet: share-records, fill-form, decline-one, any-us-core, large-response (1.9 MB), form-by-reference (GAD-7), unknown-selector, write-back (staff accept or reject each item). Supported, not yet run with a wallet: decline-all, narrowed-family, no-selector, versioned-canonical, physician-form, prefilled-form, health-card, insurance-card, shared-artifact, cross-device. Not supported: in-person-handoff. The page's "Supported use cases" table is kept current. Wallets come from the connectathon registry; health cards are accepted from any valid issuer for testing. Synthetic data only.
